### 2.1 Audit pairing caveat
`ab_launch_audit.py` pairs the Nth-from-last journal group with the
Nth-from-last line of `~/callisto_launches.log` **positionally**. That holds
only while both files are append-only and no launch bypassed Steam (which would
add a journal group with no log line). The overlay flags it prints are read
from the journal itself, so they cross-check the pairing — they matched the log
line's switches on all six. A reviewer should re-run the audit before trusting
any row.

## 3. Scenes, character and masks

The **new character** (paler, freckled, hair off the cheeks) is used for every
scene from 13:18 on, chosen by the user because more skin is visible. E0 has
her for **S1 only**; E0's S2/S3 are the previous character.

| scene | what | E0 new char | E1 new char |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | direct sun, exterior badlands | yes 12:59 | yes 13:19 |
| S2 | bounce-lit teal interior, no direct light | **no** | yes 13:25 |
| S3 | grazing, dim exterior at dusk, dark bg | **no** | yes 13:28 |

E0 S2/S3 on the new character are needed only for **E6** (`45` §3 compares E6
against E1 *and* E0); E2–E5 compare against E1 alone, which is complete.

`45` §2 wanted S3 to be a lit room at ~80°. Not reproducible: photo-mode light
sources do not load consistently. A dim exterior at dusk is the repeatable
substitute and is arguably better — a darkening term is most readable against a
dark ground. It is also the scene where every result so far inverts (§5.3).

Masks are per-scene, built once, reused for every rung, and **must be inspected
before use**. S1/S2 come from `ab_compare.py`'s connected-component growth.
**S3 is hand-built from face geometry** (`masks/S3.npy`, forehead + both cheeks
+ nose bridge, eyes/brows/lips/nose-ring excluded): it is too dim and
high-gradient for luminance growth, which leaked to 94% of the crop. An earlier
S2-style ellipse mask put the "chin" ellipse on the lips and a cheek ellipse on
hair; that was caught by rendering the mask, not by any number.

## 4. Method

### 4.1 Why not just difference the frames
Between two launches the PT sample sequence, the denoiser's temporal history
and the background NPCs all differ. On S2, measured:

| measured over | dLum (E1−E0) | sd |
|---|---|---|
| raw rectangle over the face | −0.14 | **6.10** |
| segmented skin | +0.07 | 1.07 |
| ctrl ceiling | −0.03 | 6.08 |
| ctrl wall L | −0.06 | 7.55 |
| ctrl floor R | −0.12 | 1.01 |

A rectangle's mean is dominated by hair strands, silhouette edges and
background. **Any skin delta below ~0.3/255 is inside the spread of the
non-skin controls** and means nothing. Masks are built from the **baseline**
frame only, so they cannot be biased by the effect being measured.

### 4.2 What the metrics are for
- **Mean dLum**, reported as a **% of the region mean** — skin sits at lum ~95
  (S1), ~31 (S2), ~60 (S3), so /255 numbers are not comparable across scenes.
- **Grazing bins** (distance to the mask silhouette). Every skin term here
  (`c1` Fresnel, `dcouple`, `micro_k`) is a function of NoV/NoL and must peak
  at the edge. A flat or reversed gradient means the term is not reaching those
  pixels, whatever the mean says. This is the test that found §6.1.
- **Texture energy** (`ab_texture.py`) — high-pass std inside the mask. Added
  after the user's verdict on `rough-1.3` (§5.2) could not be explained by any
  mean. This turned out to be the metric that matches perception.
- Alignment is checked every run. Photo mode reproduces the camera exactly:
  every pair phase-correlates to `0,0` with peak/sd 190–1240.

### 4.3 KNOWN DEFECT: `--tone` bins are biased, and are kept that way

`ab_compare.py --tone` assigns pixels to bins by the **baseline** image's own
luminance and then reports (test − baseline) per bin. The baseline's per-pixel
noise therefore drives bin assignment and the difference is anti-correlated
with it: pixels that landed in a low bin partly *because* they were noisily
dark show a spuriously positive delta, and the top bin a spuriously negative
one. **Regression to the mean.** Binning by the test image flips the artefact.

This has NOT been fixed, deliberately — the `--tone` numbers quoted in §5 are
what the shipped script produces, and a reviewer must be able to reproduce
them. `dev/ab_bias_check.py` quantifies the bias instead, by re-binning on a
smoothed baseline (tone is low-frequency, PT noise is high-frequency, so
smoothing decorrelates assignment from noise without destroying the lit/shadow
structure). Where the smoothed rows agree with the raw row, the finding is
real. Where they do not, the raw row is an artefact. Results, S1, 6 bins:

| binning | q1 | q2 | q3 | q4 | q5 | q6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E1−E0**, raw baseline | +1.32% | +0.82% | −0.02% | −0.34% | +0.62% | +0.78% |
| E1−E0, raw test (flipped) | −0.69% | +0.04% | +0.35% | +0.58% | +0.86% | +1.12% |
| E1−E0, smoothed σ=8 | +0.26% | +0.24% | +0.05% | +0.30% | +0.71% | +1.06% |
| E1−E0, smoothed σ=32 | +0.16% | +0.29% | −0.02% | +0.13% | +1.00% | +1.02% |
| **E2a−E1**, raw baseline | +2.17% | +1.71% | +1.48% | +1.70% | +1.71% | +0.44% |
| E2a−E1, smoothed σ=8 | +2.01% | +1.65% | +1.65% | +1.62% | +1.77% | +0.45% |
| E2a−E1, smoothed σ=32 | +1.93% | +1.51% | +1.75% | +1.91% | +1.63% | +0.39% |
| **E2b−E1**, raw baseline | +2.07% | +1.64% | +1.45% | +1.60% | +1.28% | +0.79% |
| E2b−E1, smoothed σ=8 | +1.89% | +1.55% | +1.61% | +1.56% | +1.34% | +0.80% |

So: **the E2a/E2b tone shapes survive** — stable to within ~0.2 pp across all
σ, including the characteristic drop in the top bin. **The E1−E0 shape does
not.** An earlier draft of this document claimed E1 "darkens shadowed skin
−1.05% and brightens lit skin +1.20%, increasing facial contrast". That was the
artefact. Unbiased, E1 is **+0.2…+0.3% on dark skin rising to ~+1.0% on bright
skin** — a mild contrast increase with no darkening anywhere. §6.2 is corrected
accordingly.

### 4.4 Other things wrong with this method
- **No measured noise floor.** No two launches share a config *and* a scene, so
  the floor is inferred from non-skin controls, not measured. Any future result
  in the 0.1–0.5/255 range needs a same-config repeat before it is believed.
- **E1 is not a single variable.** It enables `skin`, `shadowcull`, `ptq`,
  `ptrefl`, `ptmsggx` together. Every "E1" number is the whole stack. A
  `tier=1 skin=off` launch isolates the skin BRDF and has not been run.
- **n is not independent.** ~90k pixels, but the denoiser correlates neighbours
  heavily, so the effective sample size is far smaller than n and no p-value is
  quoted anywhere. Control regions are the null, not a t-test.
- **Session drift is unmodelled.** The ~+1.5% mid-tone lift common to *both*
  E2 rungs (§5.1) is unattributed — the controls do not support calling it
  drift (§9 c3) and no same-config repeat exists to call it real. Only the
  *difference between* the two rungs is safe.
- **One character, one save, one time of day.** Nothing here generalises to
  other skin tones; `micro_k` in particular scales with (1 − luminance) and this
  character is pale.

## 5. Results

### 5.1 Means (`reproduce.sh` §1–2)
> **SUPERSEDED by §11.2.** Every S1 figure in this table is under the L1
> noise floor (+1.232). The c3 "unattributed" question is answered: the
> common component is the floor. The **highlight separation** at the end of
> this section is the part that survives (§11.3).


| pair | scene | n | dLum /255 | % of skin mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E0 → E1 | S1 | 89945 | +0.490 | +0.52% |
| E0 → E1 | S2 *(old char)* | 94963 | +0.072 | +0.24% |
| E1 → E2a `rough-1.3` | S1 | 89945 | +1.334 | **+1.40%** |
| E1 → E2b `gloss-0.7` | S1 | 89945 | +1.302 | **+1.37%** |
| E1 → E2a | S2 | 99082 | +0.168 | +0.55% |
| E1 → E2b | S2 | 99082 | +0.200 | +0.66% |
| E1 → E2a | S3 | 57883 | −0.106 | −0.17% |
| E1 → E2b | S3 | 57883 | −0.284 | −0.47% |

The two E2 rungs have nearly identical **means** (+1.40% vs +1.37% on S1)
despite being opposite roughness directions — the mean is the wrong instrument.
But §9 c3: calling the common part *drift* is **not supported by the
controls**, which moved only ±0.26% on the same pairs. Either both rungs
really do brighten skin ~equally (a denoiser response to any α change is
plausible), or the drift is face-specific (the sun moved ~30 min between
captures; sky/dirt controls cannot proxy sun-on-face). The A-B-A relaunch
(§9.4 L1) measures it; until then the common component is **unattributed**.

Where the directions do separate is the **highlight** — top 3% of baseline skin
tone:

| scene | `rough-1.3` | `gloss-0.7` |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | **−0.81%** | **+2.14%** |
| S2 | −0.58% | −0.60% |
| S3 | −6.07% | −6.88% |

S1 mirrors as physics requires: rougher spreads the specular lobe and dims the
peak, glossier tightens and brightens it. The user independently reported
*"the highlights seem brighter"* going `rough-1.3` → `gloss-0.7`, agreeing with
the sign before seeing the number. (Both figures share `--tone`'s bias, §4.3;
the ~3 pp **separation** between them is the robust part, not the signs.)

### 5.2 Texture — the metric that matched perception (`reproduce.sh` §3)
> **SUPERSEDED by §11.2.** The S1 floor on this metric is +58.5% (vs E1).
> Every row below is inside it. The metric is sound and the bias caveat was
> irrelevant; it simply has no resolving power in this scene.


The user's unprompted verdict on `rough-1.3` was *"like actually turning
details back on the character. Like a detail filter. I can see everything."*
Its mean shift is +1.40%, which cannot explain that. High-pass energy inside
the skin mask can:

| S1 direct sun | fine | mid | coarse | rms% | fine vs E0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E0 vanilla | 2.386 | 3.812 | 5.696 | 6.353 | — |
| E1 shipping default | 2.007 | 3.367 | 5.300 | 6.047 | **−15.9%** |
| E2a `rough-1.3` | 3.222 | 4.605 | 6.324 | 6.961 | **+35.0%** |
| E2b `gloss-0.7` | 3.533 | 4.907 | 6.568 | 6.994 | **+48.1%** |

vs E1 rather than E0 that is **+60.5%** and **+76.0%**. This metric is a
within-image statistic and is *not* affected by §4.3's binning bias.

### 5.3 The other two scenes invert
> **PARTLY SUPERSEDED by §11.2.** The S2 column stands (floor −0.4%). The
> S3 column does not: the null relaunch alone gives −25.6%.


| | S2 bounce-lit | S3 dim grazing |
|---|---|---|
| `rough-1.3` fine texture | +2.3% | **−16.6%** |
| `gloss-0.7` fine texture | −1.8% | **−25.4%** |

S2 barely moves, consistent with §6.1: the α rewrite does not meaningfully
reach GI paths either. S3 **reverses** — both rungs *destroy* detail in dim
light, gloss more so. No rung has yet been shown to help outside direct sun.

## 6. Findings

### 6.1 Tier-1 `c1` does not reach bounce-lit skin — `42` reopens
**Confidence: high** *(for the S2 null; the S1 half was overstated — §9 c1)*.
S1's actual grazing profile is +0.461/+0.541/+0.582/**+0.731**/+0.502/+0.396 —
a shallow hump peaking at 14–22 px, **not** an edge-max; weak positive
evidence only. The strong half is S2 (bounce-lit): the signature is
**reversed** and monotonic over six bins with flat variance, −0.149 at the
silhouette rising to +0.151 face-on, where the retro term alone predicts
≈ +1.3/255 at the edge (§9 c1). It survives eroding the mask 4 px further
(−0.068 → +0.155), so it is not a silhouette artefact — and no
diffuse-Fresnel term can produce a reversed edge profile.
The S1 difference heatmap shows coherent structure following the pore/freckle
texture; the S2 heatmap's face is flat black with every bright edge in the
background.

This is `45` §4's *"S2 == E0 while S1 differs"* row, but the question is
sharper than `42` framed it: **the modules were served** — 77/77 unique `.dxil`
HITs on both E1 launches — so the splice is present but its effect is not.
§9 c2 claimed the two phi-lifted modules are `99bb7c26` **and** `ab0bc2fe` —
"the two GI resolvers" — so "the lift missed the dispatching module" is
excluded. **§12 corrects this: `ab0bc2fe` writes an integer index buffer, not
radiance. Only `99bb7c26` can put c1 on a pixel, and the exclusion does not
hold.** Three
hypotheses remain: (a) the guard phi's class-0 path is what these pixels
actually take (fetch skipped ⇒ gate reads 0 — `42`'s own "safe to gate on"
note describes exactly this case); (b) this scene's GI resolve happens in a
module outside the 77 anchored ones; (c) the term is present but attenuated
below the floor by the denoiser. One `skinspec=probe-cls` launch in the S2
interior separates them (§9.4 L2).
*Falsified by:* a launch where S2's grazing gradient turns edge-positive.
*Caveat:* the S2 pair is the **old character** (both frames). Not yet repeated.

### 6.2 The shipping default's skin effect is near-threshold — and it costs detail
> **The "costs detail" half is DEAD (§11.2)** — −15.9% is inside a +58.5%
> floor. The `ptclamp` hypothesis it motivated has no observation left to
> explain, and L3 is dropped (§11.6). The near-threshold half is untouched.

**Confidence: medium-high.** E1 vs E0 on S1 is +0.52% in the mean and, binned
without the §4.3 bias, +0.2…+0.3% on dark skin rising to ~+1.0% on bright skin.
That is at or below what a viewer resolves. `CURRENT.md` lists tier-1 `c1`
under *"Ships and is confirmed on screen"*; **this measurement does not support
that wording.**

Worse, E1 has **−15.9% fine texture energy vs bit-exact vanilla** (§5.2). The
shipping default makes skin measurably *smoother* than no mod at all.
*Prime suspect:* `ptclamp`, the firefly clamp — bright outliers on skin **are**
the pore and freckle speculars. Untested; needs one `tier=1 ptclamp=off`
launch. `ptbounce`/`ptrefl`/`ptmsggx` and the `c1` term itself are alternatives
and are not separable without further single-variable launches.
*Confounded by:* §4.4 — E1 is five features at once.

### 6.3 The roughness axis works, and it is a texture effect
**Confidence: high**, and the only finding with independent visual
confirmation. The α rewrite (`44` §3.1) is hitting the right ids: the two
directions mirror in the highlight (§5.1) and both massively raise fine texture
(§5.2). The user saw `rough-1.3` unprompted and described it as a detail
filter. `gloss-0.7` has more fine energy (+76% vs +60% over E1) and brighter
highlights; `rough-1.3` dims them.

**Direction not yet chosen** — the user deferred, correctly: it is an aesthetic
call and `45` only needs it at E6. The risk on `gloss-0.7` is that tighter
highlights tip toward the oily/plastic look `33` §2's ladder got wrong; the
risk on `rough-1.3` is leaving detail on the table.
*Open:* both cost detail in dim light (§5.3), which neither `44` nor `45`
predicted and which no rung addresses.

## 7. What has not been done

- **E3 `couple`, E4 `micro`, E5 eyes, E6 `real`/`real-gloss`** — not launched.
- **E7 kernel presets, E8 sun size, E9 SER, E10 RR-off, E11 probe decode** —
  not launched. E10 has risen in priority: everything measured sits between
  0.5% and 2.5% in the mean, and if Ray Reconstruction is flattening these the
  whole ladder is being judged through it.
- **`tier=1 skin=off`** — the control that would deconfound every E1 number.
- **`tier=1 ptclamp=off`** — the test for §6.2's detail loss.
- **A same-config repeat** — the only way to get a real noise floor (§4.4).
- **E0 S2/S3 on the current character** — needed for E6, not before.

## 8. Where a reviewer should attack this first

1. **§4.3.** The bias is real and I kept it. Decide whether the `--tone` rows
   in §5.1 should be quoted at all, or replaced wholesale by `ab_bias_check`'s
   smoothed rows.
2. **§6.2's causal claim.** "`ptclamp` eats pore speculars" is a hypothesis
   with zero evidence behind it beyond plausibility. It is stated as a suspect,
   but it is the kind of claim this project has historically promoted to fact.
3. **The S2 old-character pair.** §6.1 — a high-confidence finding — rests on a
   capture pair of a character no longer used, from two different sessions.
4. **Mask sensitivity.** No result is reported against an alternative mask.
   The S3 mask in particular is hand-drawn ellipses chosen by eye.
5. **§5.1's drift explanation.** "The common +1.5% is session drift" is
   inferred, not measured, and it is doing real work in the argument.


## 9. Peer review (2026-08-30 evening, Fable)

Method: re-ran `reproduce.sh` end to end (exit 0, **every §5 figure
matched**), re-derived the S2 grazing table from the raw pair, viewed the S1
quartet and the S2 mask/heatmap, checked mask sensitivity (below), and
checked the build reports for which modules carry the phi-lifted gate.

### 9.1 Verdicts on §8's attack points

1. **§4.3 tone bias** — handling is sound; the smoothed-baseline rows are the
   quotable ones from now on. The raw rows stay in §5.1 for reproducibility
   with the shared-bias caveat already attached. No further action.
2. **§6.2's `ptclamp` suspect** — correctly labelled a hypothesis; stays one
   until L3. The −15.9% itself is *not* a mask artefact: eroding the mask 4
   and 8 px moves it only to −15.5% / −14.9%. It *is* a single pair with no
   floor.
3. **The S2 old-character pair** — internally clean (aligns 0,0, controls
   flat) and the reversed gradient survives 4 px of extra erosion
   (−0.068 edge → +0.155 interior). The finding stands as *"no c1 signature
   on bounce-lit skin"*; the amended §6.1 no longer claims more.
4. **Mask sensitivity** — checked, passes: S1 means shift ≤0.08/255 and
   texture ratios ≤1.5 pp under 4–8 px erosion. The hand-built S3 mask stays
   the weakest artefact; acceptable while every S3 claim is directional.
5. **§5.1 drift** — the one real reasoning error found; corrected in place
   (c3). The conclusion (don't trust the means) survives; the mechanism
   claimed for it didn't.

### 9.2 Corrections applied in place

- **c1** §6.1: the S1 grazing quote skipped the +0.731 peak at 14–22 px; the
  profile is a hump, not an edge-max — S1 is weak evidence, the S2 null is
  the finding. Expected magnitude added: with `rho_r=1.25, n_r/m_r=0.75`,
  the retro term at the silhouette (NoV→0, NoL≈0.5) is ≈ +4.5% of a 31-lum
  region ≈ **+1.4/255**; measured **−0.15**. Absent or >90% suppressed.
- **c2** §6.1: attribution narrowed to three hypotheses; "lift missed the
  module" excluded (both GI resolvers carry the phi gate — verified in the
  build reports). **WRONG — see §12: `ab0bc2fe` is not a GI resolver. It
  writes integer sample indices, not colour. There is one colour-writing
  resolver in the anchored set, not two, and hypothesis (b) is stronger than
  this exclusion implied.**
- **c3** §5.1/§4.4: "drift" demoted to "unattributed"; the controls
  contradict the drift story rather than supporting it.

### 9.3 Additional review notes (no text amended)

- **Texture (§5.2) conflates authored detail with residual noise.** A
  tighter lobe raises specular sample variance, so part of `gloss-0.7`'s
  +48% is plausibly sparkle, not pores; `rough-1.3`'s +35% is the
  mechanistically trustworthy one (roughening cannot add specular variance —
  it reduces veiling glare over the albedo texture). This asymmetry matters
  for the fork (§9.5). L1/L4 calibrate the metric.
- **§5.3's "S3 destroys detail" should read "S3 dims interior speculars".**
  The S3 grazing tables show the E2 deltas are ~0 at the edge and grow
  *face-on* (−0.30 rough / −0.54 gloss at 35+ px): dim-light highlight loss,
  not edge-detail destruction. Physically expected from both α edits.
- The **E1 S1 grazing hump** (c1) is worth re-checking when L1 lands: if a
  same-shape hump appears between two identical launches, it was never
  signal.
- `LAUNCHES.md` totals (105 HITs vs 102 unique) are re-serves; fine.
- 02/03's "c1 confirmed on screen" vs §6.2's near-threshold E1: not yet a
  contradiction — different era, build, scene, character — but `CURRENT`
  now carries the caveat instead of the bare claim.

### 9.4 The queue, revised — calibration before more rungs

Everything measured so far sits at 0.2–2.5% in the mean with no noise floor
and one denoiser. Four single-launch controls fix that; run them in order,
before E3–E6:

| # | config (delta vs E1) | scenes | answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1** | none — exact E1 relaunch (A-B-A) | S1,S2,S3 | the noise floor for mean/tone/texture; whether §5.1's common +1.4% and §5.2's −15.9% survive |
| **L2** | `skinspec=probe-cls` | S2 interior | §6.1: skin painted ⇒ the class gate passes on bounce-lit skin (hypothesis c; `42` stays closed); not painted ⇒ run `probe-sub` to split gate-fails (a) from wrong-module (b) |
| **L3** | `ptclamp=off` (journal will read `ptq=rbm`) | S1 | §6.2: does the firefly clamp eat pore speculars |
| **L4** | none; toggle Ray Reconstruction OFF in the game's own settings | S1,S3 | how much of every number is the denoiser (`43` M1) |

Caveats: L2's paint sites are the radiance writes, not the c1 lines, but
they hang off the same class anchor, so a painted face clears the gate for
both. L3 changes the ptq combo — expected; `ser=off`, nothing goes stale.
L4 may need photo-mode settings re-pinned.

Then: **E3 `couple` → E4 `micro` → E5 `eyes-wet`** (one launch each, S1+S3,
now interpretable against L1's floor), re-shoot **E0 S2/S3 on the current
character**, then **E6** with the direction chosen per §9.5.

### 9.5 The fork: recommendation
> **SUPERSEDED by §11.5.** Arguments 2 and 4 rested on S1/S3 texture numbers
> that are now known to be floor. The recommendation survives; its basis does
> not.


**Do not pick a direction yet — L1 through L4 are cheaper than a wrong pick,
and two of them can flip the texture numbers the pick would rest on.**

If a direction must be named today: **`rough-1.3`**. In order: the user's
unprompted perception ("detail filter") is the only human data point and it
landed there; its texture gain is the mechanistically trustworthy one (§9.3 —
gloss's gain is partly sparkle until L4 says otherwise); `gloss-0.7` walks
toward the `33` §2 wet-plastic failure the oily ladder already committed;
and in the one scene where both hurt (S3 dim), gloss hurts more (−25.4% vs
−16.6% fine, −0.54 vs −0.30 face-on). `rough-1.6` stays untested as the
ceiling probe if E6-with-1.3 still reads plastic.

The S3 regression is the open question neither direction answers: both rungs
dim dim-light skin. If L1 shows S3's numbers are real (not floor), the fix
is a *conditional* axis (e.g. scale toward 1.0 as irradiance falls) — a new
build and doc, not a reason to stall E6.

## 11. L1 — the noise floor, and what it destroys

> **PARTLY WITHDRAWN — read §13 first.** The *verdicts* below mostly survive,
> but the floor figure is wrong: §11 attributed to launch noise what §13 shows
> is a global renderer change between 13:28 and 13:36. The real within-regime
> floor is ~1% in the mean and ~6% on skin texture, not +58.5%. §11.4 is
> withdrawn outright, and §11.2's kill of §6.2 is reversed by §13.3.

One launch, 2026-08-30 14:45:50, **zero config delta** vs the 13:18:10 E1
launch (`skin_sha=0d0f3ee45ea0d538`, `payload=225acb871d94a4b8`, 77/12/10/3
HITs, 0 `ser_reject` — byte-identical serve; `a-b-testing/L1-noise-floor/`).
Same save, same camera: S1 and S2 phase-correlate to 0,0, S3 to (0,−1).

Numbers: `bash a-b-testing/reproduce.sh` §5.

### 11.1 The floor, beside the effects it is supposed to underwrite

| metric | scene | **floor (E1→L1, no change)** | the effects `46` measured |

| mean `dLum` | S1 | **+1.232** | E0→E1 +0.490 · E2a +1.334 · E2b +1.302 |
| mean `dLum` | S2 | **−0.061** | E2a +0.168 · E2b +0.200 |
| mean `dLum` | S3 | **−0.020** | E2a −0.106 · E2b −0.284 |

In S1 and S3 the null relaunch moves every metric **further than any rung

### 11.2 Dead — do not quote these again

- **§5.1's S1 means, all of them.** E0→E1's +0.52% and both E2 rungs'
  ~+1.4% are under a +1.29% floor. c3's "unattributed common component" is
  now attributed: it *is* the floor. Not drift, not a denoiser response to
  α — it is what two byte-identical launches do.
- **§5.2's whole S1 texture table.** The E1 row's **−15.9%** and E2a's
  **+35.0%** sit inside a floor of +33.4% (E0-referenced). L1 and E2a land
  1.3% apart (3.182 vs 3.222) while E1 and L1 — the *identical* pair — land
  58% apart. §5.2's "this metric is not affected by §4.3's bias" was true
  and irrelevant; the bias was never its problem.
- **§5.3's S3 inversion.** Both rungs' "destroys detail" (−16.6%, −25.4%)
  are at or under the −25.6% floor. So is §9.3's rewrite of it
  ("dims interior speculars", −0.30/−0.54 face-on vs a −0.243 floor bin).
- **§6.2's "the shipping default costs 15.9% of skin texture".** Gone, and
  with it the only observation `ptclamp` was ever suspected of causing.
- **§9.3's asymmetry argument** (rough's +35% mechanistically trustworthy,
  gloss's +48% partly sparkle). Both are floor; there is nothing to be
  asymmetric about.
- **§9.5 arguments 2 and 4** — see §11.5.
- **§9.3's grazing-hump re-check**, resolved: the floor's S1 profile is a
  flat +1.0…+1.3 with its *minimum* at 14–22 px, where E1's +0.731 peak
  was. Different shape, but a +0.73 peak riding a +1.2 floor was never
  readable either way. S1 grazing is not an instrument.

### 11.3 Alive, and now with a floor behind it

- **Everything in S2.** Floor −0.061 mean, −0.4% texture, ±0.10 per grazing
  bin. §6.1's finding — no c1 signature on bounce-lit skin, −0.15 measured
  against a ≈+1.4 prediction — is **real**: the prediction was 14× the floor
  and the measurement is at it. `42` stays reopened, and L2 is still the
  launch that decides it.
- **Rung-vs-rung differentials in S1.** The floor is a near-*uniform
  relative* offset (+1.6/+1.3/+1.3/+1.4/+1.4/+1.0% by smoothed baseline
  tone), so it cancels in a rung-to-rung difference. Measured directly,
  E2a→E2b: whole-face **−0.032** (controls +0.03/−0.04/+0.00 — flat), while
  the **top-3% highlight bin moves +5.756 = +3.23%**. A flat face with a
  moving specular peak is a signature the floor does not produce.
  §5.1's call — *"the ~3 pp separation is the robust part, not the signs"* —
  was correct. It is now the only quantitative S1 result standing.

### 11.4 Mechanism: it is the denoiser resolving different pores

The E1→L1 diff heatmaps (S1 and S3) are dense **pore-scale speckle over the
entire face**, with colour fringing at high-contrast edges (eyelashes, the
nose ring). There is no shadow-edge structure, no hair displacement, no
geometry motion, and the static controls are flat (S1 ceiling −0.054, floor
−0.171). The sun did not move and the camera did not move. What differs
between two identical launches is *which micro-detail Ray Reconstruction
decided to resolve* — which is exactly what a fine-high-pass metric measures.

This also explains the scene split: S2 is interior bounce light with no
strong speculars and little for RR to disagree about, so its floor is ~0.
S1 (direct sun) and S3 (dim, high-ISO-like) are where RR works hardest.

### 11.5 The fork, re-derived

`46` §9.5 recommended `rough-1.3` on four arguments. Two are now dead
(its texture gain; gloss hurting S3 more). Two survive:

1. the user's unprompted *"like a detail filter"* on `rough-1.3` — the only
   human data point, and unaffected by any of this;
2. `gloss-0.7` walks toward the `33` §2 wet-plastic failure.

Plus one new one, pointing the other way: the surviving S1 measurement says
gloss brightens the specular peak +3.2% and rough dims it — i.e. the metric
now confirms *the axis works*, without saying which end is right.

**Recommendation unchanged (`rough-1.3`), confidence lower, and the reason
has changed**: it now rests on one human observation and one a-priori
argument, not on numbers. Do not spend launches defending it. The user's eye
is the instrument for this question; `46`'s metrics were never able to answer
it and are now known not to be.

### 11.6 The queue, revised again

> **SUPERSEDED by §13.4** — L3 is reinstated, and L4 never actually ran (RR
> was still on; `DLSS_D: true`).

| # | status | why |
|---|---|---|
| **L2** `skinspec=probe-cls`, S2 | **run it** | unchanged; S2 is the one trustworthy scene and §6.1 survives |
| **L3** `ptclamp=off`, S1 | **drop** | its only motivation was §6.2's −15.9%, which was floor. Nothing left to explain, and S1 cannot measure the answer anyway |
| **L4** RR off | **promote, and make it two launches** | it no longer merely quantifies the denoiser's share — it decides whether S1/S3 can measure anything at all. One RR-off launch gives the RR *effect*; the floor needs **two** RR-off launches at E1 config (S1+S3 each) |

Then, and only if L4's RR-off floor is small: re-baseline E1 and re-shoot E2
under RR-off before E3–E6. If it is still large, S1 and S3 are abandoned as
measurement scenes and the programme runs on **S2 means + S1 rung-vs-rung
differentials**, with the user's eye as the arbiter of direction.

Standing rule this adds to `GOTCHAS`: **a rung is not measured until a null
relaunch of the same config has been measured in the same scene with the
same metric.** Six launches of numbers were published before one was.

## 12. `ab0bc2fe` is not a GI resolver — §9 c2 mis-identified it

Found while pre-flighting L2, before the launch. `skin.set/probe-cls` has
**76** modules where every skin rung has 77. The one it declines is
`ab0bc2fee876d489` — which §9 c2 named as one of "the two GI resolvers" and
used to *exclude* the "lift missed the module" hypothesis.

### 12.1 What was measured (static, no launch needed)

Reproduce: `spirv-dis ~/callisto_dump/ab0bc2fee876d489.dxil.spv` and
`python3 dev/patch_subtype_probe.py <asm> --tier cls --outdir /tmp/x`
→ `error: no image write reachable for the hunt`.

| fact | `ab0bc2fe` | `99bb7c26` (the other) |
|---|---|---|
| sole `OpImageWrite` target | `OpTypeImage %int 2D … 2` (int storage) | float 2D |
| value written | `OpCompositeConstruct %v4uint` → `OpBitcast %v4int` | `OpCompositeConstruct %v4float` |
| components | `(a, b, a, a)`, each `OpSelect(valid, RoundEven→ConvertFToS(f), 0xFFFFFFFF)` | radiance floats |
| guards on those values | `OpIsInf`/`OpIsNan` on the float, `OpULessThan … %uint_2`, a `&255`+1 byte counter | none |
| workgroup / subgroup use | LDS, `%SubgroupSize`, `LocalSize 32 16 1` | none, `LocalSize` plain |
| in `swaps.skin` (tier-1 c1 installed) | **yes** | yes |
| paintable by `probe-cls` | **no** | yes |

Census of the anchored set: **76 of 77 write `v4float`; exactly one writes
`v4uint` — this module.**

### 12.2 What it means

A rounded integer with an "invalid" sentinel, bounds-checked, carrying an
age/count byte, written to an int storage image at a pixel coordinate, is a
**sample-index / reservoir buffer** — a ReSTIR-style "which sample do I reuse
here" pass. It evaluates the full material stack (which is why the 1/pi +
0.107508637 anchor matched it) in order to compute a reuse *weight*, and then
writes **indices, not colour**.

So:

- **§9 c2 is corrected.** There is one GI *resolver* among the anchored
  modules that can put c1 on a pixel, not two. "The lift reached both
  resolvers" is not the reassurance it was read as.
- The tier-1 `c1` splice **is** installed in `ab0bc2fe` (it is in
  `swaps.skin`), where it can only perturb sample-reuse weighting. It cannot
  brighten a pixel directly. Whether that is harmless or a subtle bias on
  which samples survive is untested and not currently worth a launch.
- **§6.1's hypothesis (b) is stronger than §9 left it.** For c1 to reach
  bounce-lit skin, `99bb7c26` (or another of the 76 colour-writers) has to be
  what shades those pixels.

### 12.3 What it does to L2 — run it, the reading is *cleaner*

The instinct on finding the gap was that L2 is now a false-negative trap:
the probe cannot paint `ab0bc2fe`, so a red-less face would be ambiguous.
It is not, because `ab0bc2fe` **cannot paint by any mechanism** — it has no
colour output to tint. It is not a candidate explanation for an unpainted
face. L2 reads:

| S2 interior under `skinspec=probe-cls` | conclusion |
|---|---|
| face goes **red** (class 1 = red, `HUNT_PALETTE`) | the class gate passes in a colour-writing anchored module ⇒ §6.1 hypothesis (c), term present but suppressed below the floor. `42` closes. |
| face **not** red | the pixels are not shaded by any of the 76 colour-writers with class 1 ⇒ (a) gate reads something else, or (b) an unanchored module. Then `probe-sub` per §9.4. (b) is now the favourite. |

Caveat unchanged from §9.4: the paint sites are the radiance writes, not the
c1 lines, but they hang off the same class anchor.

Standing lesson for `GOTCHAS`: **"the module carries the patch" is not
"the patch can reach a pixel."** Check what the module *writes* before
building an argument on its coverage. A module can carry the whole BRDF and
emit nothing but indices.

## 13. §11 was wrong about *why* — there is a regime break at ~13:30

L4a (15:37:29) was meant to be the RR-off arm. It was not: `DLSS_D: true` in
`…/AppData/Local/CD Projekt Red/Cyberpunk 2077/UserSettings.json`, written
15:43:25 at that session's exit. So L4a is a **third RR-on sample at E1
config** — and three samples show what two could not.

### 13.1 The measurement that breaks §11

Fine texture energy **outside** the skin mask — sky, terrain, buildings, which
no skin rung can touch (`--mask` inverted; `reproduce.sh` §6):

| capture | time | non-skin fine | vs E0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| E0 vanilla | 12:59 | 5.881 | — |
| E1 default | 13:19 | 5.721 | −2.7% |
| E2a `rough-1.3` | 13:38 | 6.583 | **+11.9%** |
| E2b `gloss-0.7` | 13:53 | 6.987 | **+18.8%** |
| L1 `off` | 14:47 | 6.600 | **+12.2%** |
| L4a `off` | 15:39 | 6.785 | **+15.4%** |

**Something in the renderer changed globally between 13:28 and 13:36** — after
the E1 capture set, before the E2a launch — and stayed changed. Static
geometry gained 12–19% fine energy. Nothing in this mod can do that. The
leading suspect is a graphics-settings change (DLSS preset Legacy↔Transformer,
or `DLSS_NewSharpness`, currently 0.25); unconfirmed, the file records only
current state.

Call pre-13:30 **regime A** (E0, E1) and post-13:30 **regime B** (E2a, E2b,
L1, L2, L4a). **Cross-regime comparisons are confounded.** That is every
E1→E2 number in §5.

### 13.2 The real floor, measured within regime B (L1 → L4a)

| metric | S1 | S2 | S3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean `dLum` | +0.166 (sd 4.18) | +0.043 (sd 1.04) | +0.449 (sd 2.59) |
| tone bins, worst | +1.14 … −0.95% | +1.49 … −1.41% | +1.02 … −1.50% |
| fine texture, skin | +6.1% | — | +9.3% |
| fine texture, non-skin | +2.8% | — | — |

So the floor is **~1% in the mean and ~6% on skin texture**, not §11's +58.5%.
§11.1's table conflated the floor with the regime break, and §11.4's "Ray
Reconstruction resolves different pores" was read off a heatmap that spans the
break. **§11.4 is withdrawn** — the pore-speckle diff it describes is at least
partly the global change, and RR has still never been tested.

### 13.3 What that does to §11's verdicts

- **§5.2's E2 texture gains: still dead, better reason.** Re-measured inside
  regime B against both nulls, with a non-skin control: skin-specific movement
  is `rough-1.3` +1.4 pp and `gloss-0.7` +5.1 pp against a null-to-null
  +3.3 pp. Neither separates. Not a 58% floor — a ~6% floor plus a
  contaminated baseline.
- **§5.1's E2 means: still dead**, same reason (E1 is the cross-regime
  baseline).
- **§11.3 stands, and is now better supported.** S2's floor is +0.043 with a
  within-regime null. The E2a→E2b differential (both regime B) gives a flat
  face and **+3.23%** on the top-3% highlight against a null top-bin of
  **−0.95%** — 3.4× the null and opposite in sign.
- **§6.2 and L3: NOT dead — un-tested.** §11.2 killed the −15.9% using a
  cross-regime floor, which was invalid. E0→E1 is **within regime A**: skin
  −15.9% against a non-skin −2.7%, i.e. −13.2 pp skin-specific. There is no
  regime-A null to compare it against, so it is unproven, not disproven.
  **L3 goes back in the queue**, behind an E0-config re-shoot in the current
  regime.

### 13.4 Queue, third revision

| # | what | why |
|---|---|---|

## 14. L5 — the first valid mod-vs-vanilla measurement

2026-08-30T16:08:20, `tier=off kernel=off` → journal `ptq=off skin=off
tier=off payload=d2dfb3f53119172b`, **0 HITs, bit-exact vanilla** — the same
payload fingerprint as the 12:38 E0 launch. Filed in
`a-b-testing/L5-vanilla-regimeB/`.

Captured while intending an RR-off launch; `DLSS_D` reads `false` afterwards.
**RR was still on during the captures**: S1 non-skin fine energy is 6.581
against L1's 6.600 (**0.3%**) on a metric where the §13 regime break moved
12–19%, and a terrain crop is visually identical in noise character to L1's.
The toggle happened after shooting. So L5 is vanilla, RR on, regime B — it
pairs with L1 and L4a, which are mod-default, RR on, regime B.

This is the first time the project has had a vanilla baseline and a mod
baseline on the same side of a regime break, with a measured floor.

### 14.1 Means — vanilla → mod default (S1 controls flat: −0.045, −0.000)

| baseline tone bin | S1 mod effect | S1 floor (L1→L4a) |
|---|---|---|
| 10.6–71.6 | +0.21% | +1.14% |
| 71.6–80.2 | +0.25% | +0.57% |
| 80.2–88.2 | +0.26% | +0.35% |
| 88.2–106.4 | +0.43% | +0.14% |
| **106.4–135.1** | **+1.83%** | +0.23% |
| **135.1–166.5** | **+1.66%** | −0.59% |
| 166.5–207.2 | +0.64% | −0.95% |

**The mod brightens only the lit half of the face**, by ~1.7–1.8% in the bins
where the floor is ~0, and does essentially nothing below ~106 luminance.

This independently reproduces **L2**. The probe showed the class gate paints
skin only above ~116 luminance (§12/L2: +0.008 below, +0.285 above). The
radiometric measurement finds the mod's effect switching on at the same
threshold, from a completely different instrument. Two methods, one boundary:
**the skin BRDF reaches directly-lit skin and nothing else.**

- **S2 bounce-lit**: `dLum` −0.259, tone bins −0.1 to −1.6% against a floor of
  +1.5 to −1.4%. At or near floor, sign inconsistent with c1's predicted
  brightening. §6.1 stands — c1 does not reach bounce-lit skin.
- **S3 dim grazing**: `dLum` −0.478, controls flat (−0.013, −0.014). The
  bright bins **darken −3.91% and −6.90%** against a floor of −0.29/−1.50%.

### 14.2 Texture — §6.2 resolved, and it inverts

Two mod samples against one vanilla sample, each with its non-skin control:

| | S1 skin | S1 non-skin | skin-specific | S3 skin | S3 non-skin | skin-specific |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L5 vanilla | ref | ref | — | ref | ref | — |
| L1 mod | +0.3% | +0.3% | **0.0 pp** | −27.7% | −9.6% | **−18.1 pp** |
| L4a mod | +6.4% | +3.1% | **+3.3 pp** | −21.0% | −9.9% | **−11.1 pp** |

- **S1: the mod costs no skin texture at all.** §6.2's headline — "the
  shipping default costs 15.9% of skin texture vs vanilla" — is now properly
  **dead**. §11.2 killed it with an invalid cross-regime floor and §13.3
  reinstated it; this measurement retires it on the evidence. In direct sun,
  vanilla and the mod are within the floor of each other.
- **S3: the mod costs a lot.** Skin loses 11–18 pp *beyond* the scene-wide
  loss, and the scene itself loses ~10% fine energy — a figure the two mod
  launches reproduce to 0.3 pp. Something in the default stack is removing
  high-frequency energy globally in dim light, and removing more of it from
  skin.

### 14.3 `ptclamp` is the suspect, and L3 now has a prediction

A firefly clamp clips bright outlier samples. In a dim, sample-starved scene
that *is* most of the high-frequency energy, and it would show up exactly as
observed: a scene-wide fine-energy loss (−10%, reproduced twice), a further
loss on the noisiest surface (skin under SSS), and the brightest tone bins
darkening (−3.9%, −6.9%) while everything else holds.

**L3 (`ptclamp=off`, S1 + S3) predicts:** S3 non-skin fine energy returns
toward vanilla's 2.689 (from ~2.43), S3 skin returns toward 2.178 (from
~1.65), the S3 bright-bin darkening shrinks, and **S1 barely moves** — the
clamp should be near-inert in bright sun. If S3 does not move, the clamp is
not the mechanism and `ptbounce`/`ptreg` are next.

Journal will read `ptq=rbm` (the clamp letter drops out of the combo);
`ser=off`, so nothing goes stale.

### 14.4 Where this leaves the roughness fork

Untouched. §11.3's surviving result — the E2a→E2b differential, flat face,
**+3.23%** on the top-3% highlight against a within-regime null of −0.95% —
is still the only quantitative separation between the two directions, and
§11.5's recommendation (`rough-1.3`, on the user's eye and the `33` §2
wet-plastic argument) still stands without numerical support. Note that E2a
and E2b were both shot in direct sun, where §14.1 now shows the BRDF actually
acts — so the fork is at least being argued in the one lighting condition
where the axis is live.

## 15. L3 — the clamp is half-guilty: it darkens, it does not blur

2026-08-30T16:26:45, `ptclamp=off`, everything else at default. Journal
`ptq=rbm` — the clamp letter dropped out of the combo exactly as §14.3 said it
would — `skin_sha=0d0f3ee45ea0d538`, 105 HITs, 0 `ser_reject`. RR was on
(toggled back before the session; S1 non-skin 6.667 sits inside the RR-on
regime-B band 6.581–6.785, so this frame is in the same regime as L1/L4a/L5).

`a-b-testing/L3-ptclamp-off/`.

### 15.1 The prediction, scored

§14.3 predicted four things. **Two failed, two partly held.**

| prediction | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| S3 non-skin fine returns toward vanilla's 2.689 | **2.441**, vs 2.431/2.424 with the clamp **on** | **FAILED — no movement at all** |
| S3 skin fine returns toward vanilla's 2.178 | 1.817, vs 1.574/1.720 | partial, and inside the clamp-on sample spread |
| S3 bright-bin darkening shrinks | −3.91→−2.30%, −6.90→−5.11% | partly held |
| S1 barely moves | non-skin +1.3%, inside the band | held |

Skin-specific fine loss (skin − non-skin): **−18.1 pp** (L1) and **−11.1 pp**
(L4a) with the clamp on, **−7.4 pp** with it off. The direction is right; the
two clamp-on samples differ from each other by 7 pp, so a 3.7 pp move off the
nearer one is not separable.

Mean, S3 skin, vanilla → mod: **−0.478** with the clamp on, **+0.153** with it
off. That part is real — the clamp costs ~0.63/255 of dim-lit skin brightness
and about 1.6–1.8 pp of the bright-bin darkening.

### 15.2 What this actually settles

- **`ptclamp` is exonerated for the detail loss.** Three mod launches with the
  clamp in two different states put S3's scene-wide fine energy at −9.6%,
  −9.9% and −9.2% against vanilla. The clamp moves it by 0.4 pp. §6.2's
  mechanism — "the firefly clamp eats pore speculars" — is **wrong**.
- **`ptclamp` is convicted of dimming dim-lit skin.** Small, real, and
  arguably the clamp doing its job; whether it is worth the brightness is a
  taste call, not a bug.
- **The −10% scene-wide fine-energy loss in dim light is unexplained and very
  stable** (three configs, 0.7 pp spread). It is scene-wide, so it is not the
  skin overlay and not the SSS kernel. Remaining: `ptreg`, `ptbounce`,
  `ptrefl`, `ptmsggx`, `shadowcull`.

### 15.3 Next: `ptreg`

Path regularization is *designed* to trade high-frequency variance for
smoothness — it widens lobes on later bounces specifically to kill noise. A
stable, scene-wide, dim-light-only loss of fine energy is what it should look
like. It is the strongest remaining candidate by mechanism, not just by
elimination.

**L6 (`ptreg=off`, clamp restored, S1 + S3) predicts:** S3 non-skin fine
energy moves substantially toward vanilla's 2.689 from ~2.43. If it does not,
the cause is `ptbounce`/`ptrefl`/`ptmsggx`/`shadowcull` and the elimination
continues.

A useful side-effect either way: L6 is a fourth mod-config sample against the
single vanilla capture. If some config finally matches vanilla's non-skin
2.689, that also retires the worry that L5 is simply an anomalous baseline —
which one sample cannot currently rule out.

## 16. L6 — `ptreg` cleared; and S3-skin turns out to be unusable

2026-08-30T16:37:33, `ptreg=off`, clamp restored. Journal `ptq=cbm` — the reg
letter dropped — 105 HITs, 0 `ser_reject`, `skin_sha=0d0f3ee45ea0d538`. RR on
during the captures (S1 non-skin 6.808, top of the RR-on band; `DLSS_D` was
toggled to `false` at 16:42:45, after both shots).
`a-b-testing/L6-ptreg-off/`.

### 16.1 `ptreg` is not the cause either

S3 scene-wide fine energy vs vanilla's 2.689:

| config | S3 non-skin | vs vanilla |
|---|---|---|
| L1 default | 2.431 | −9.6% |
| L4a default | 2.424 | −9.9% |
| L3 `ptclamp=off` | 2.441 | −9.2% |
| L6 `ptreg=off` | 2.458 | −8.6% |

**Four samples, three configs, 1.4% spread.** Turning off the two switches
most likely to smooth an image moves the number by ~1 pp each. Path
regularization is cleared on the same evidence the clamp was.

Remaining candidates for a scene-wide dim-light effect: `ptbounce`, `ptrefl`,
`ptmsggx`, `shadowcull`, or the `ptq` overlay as a whole.

### 16.2 WITHDRAWN: every S3 **skin** texture figure in §14–§15

The two identical-config launches L1 and L4a give S3 skin fine energy **1.574
and 1.720 — 9.3% apart**. The same pair gives S3 *non-skin* 2.431 and 2.424,
**0.3% apart**. S3's skin mask is small (57,883 px, 23.9% of the crop) and
sits on the noisiest surface in the dimmest scene; the metric has a ~9% floor
there and roughly zero on static geometry.

So these do not survive:

- §14.2's "skin loses 11–18 pp beyond the scene-wide loss" (−18.1 / −11.1 pp)
  — computed from S3 skin, inside its own floor.
- §15.1's "skin-specific loss −18.1 → −11.1 → −7.4 pp" trend — same.
- The ordering L6 −27.9% < L1 −27.7% < L4a −21.0% < L3 −16.6% is noise; all
  four configs are one population.

**S3 non-skin stands** (0.3% same-config floor). **S3 skin is retired as a
metric** unless the mask is enlarged or the scene is re-framed.

### 16.3 The baseline now has n=1, and today already punished that once

The mod cluster is tight (1.4%) and vanilla sits **+10.3%** above its mean.
That reads as a real effect — but it rests on **one** vanilla capture, and
`GOTCHAS` gained a rule today that says exactly this is not allowed: *a rung is
not measured until a null relaunch of the same config has been measured in the
same scene with the same metric.* §11 was written by trusting a single E1
baseline and had to be withdrawn in §13.

**L7 = vanilla repeat** (`tier=off kernel=off`, S1 + S3), before any further
switch elimination. Two outcomes:

- **L7 lands near 2.689** → the −9% is real, the vanilla side is stable, and
  the elimination continues with `ptbounce` as the next candidate (the bounce
  cull mask 1→255 puts far more geometry into indirect paths, which is the
  remaining mechanism that could smooth a dim scene scene-wide).
- **L7 lands near 2.44** → there is no mod effect at all; L5 was a fluke, and
  §14.2's "the mod costs detail in dim light" joins §6.2 and §11 in the pile
  of things one un-repeated baseline invented.

Either way it costs one launch and it is the difference between chasing a real
mechanism and chasing a sampling artefact.

## 17. L7 — the vanilla baseline replicates; the dim-light effect is real

2026-08-30T16:45:53, `tier=off kernel=off`, `payload=d2dfb3f53119172b`, 0 HITs
— the same bit-exact-vanilla fingerprint as L5. `a-b-testing/L7-vanilla-repeat/`.

### 17.1 Two clusters, no overlap

S3 scene-wide (non-skin) fine energy:

| | n | mean | spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| **vanilla** (L5, L7) | 2 | **2.708** | 1.4% |
| **mod** (L1, L4a default; L3 clamp-off; L6 reg-off) | 4 | **2.438** | 1.4% |

Difference **−9.9%**, which is **7.3×** the larger within-cluster spread, and
the clusters do not overlap — vanilla's minimum (2.689) is above the mod's
maximum (2.458). Three different mod configurations land inside one 1.4%
band; two vanilla launches land inside another.

**The shipping default removes ~10% of scene-wide fine detail in the dim
scene.** That is the first effect this project has measured with a replicated
baseline on both sides. In S1 (direct sun) the same metric shows vanilla
6.581/6.456 against mod 6.600/6.785 — overlapping. **Dim light only.**

### 17.2 What is left to blame

Not `ptclamp` (§15), not `ptreg` (§16) — each moves it ~1 pp. The enabled
overlays are `skin`, `shadowcull`, `ptq` and `ptrefl`; within `ptq` the combo
letters are r(eg), c(lamp), b(ounce), m(sggx), and r and c are cleared.

**`ptbounce` is the candidate on mechanism, not just elimination.** The bounce
cull mask goes 1→255 (`26` §4), putting far more geometry into indirect paths.
More geometry contributing to GI means better-converged, smoother indirect
light. In a dim scene indirect light *is* the image; in direct sun it is a
minor term. A scene-wide fine-energy loss that appears only in dim light is
exactly that shape.

**L8 (`ptbounce=off`, S1 + S3) predicts:** S3 non-skin moves substantially
toward 2.708 from ~2.44, and S1 stays put. Journal should read `ptq=rcm`.
If S3 does not move, the remaining suspects are `ptmsggx`, `ptrefl`,
`shadowcull` and the `skin` overlay itself — and the next step is to disable
that whole group at once and bisect, rather than one switch per launch.

### 17.3 Caveat that will matter when the culprit is found

A high-pass metric cannot tell *removed noise* from *removed detail*
(`46` §9.3 raised this for the skin rungs; it applies here too). If
`ptbounce` is the cause, the honest description may be **"the mod converges
dim-light GI better, so there is less residual sampling noise"** — an
improvement that this metric scores as a loss. The number localises the
mechanism; only the user's eye decides whether the dim scene looks better or
worse with it. Get that verdict at the same launch that identifies the
switch: shoot S3 with the switch off, and look at the two frames side by side
before writing a conclusion.

## 18. L8 — it is `ptbounce`, and it is doing its job

2026-08-30T16:53:40, `ptbounce=off`. Journal `ptq=rcm`; **served content
verified by sha, not by the journal's payload field** — `swaps.ptq` hashed
`6fe05ecc3ab345df` = `ptq/rcm/base`, correct. (See §18.3: the payload field
collided here and is not a content hash.)
`a-b-testing/L8-ptbounce-off/`.

### 18.1 The switch found

S3 scene-wide (non-skin) fine energy:

| config | S3 non-skin | vs vanilla mean (2.708) |
|---|---|---|
| vanilla L5 / L7 | 2.689 / 2.726 | — |
| default (bounce **on**) L1 / L4a | 2.431 / 2.424 | −10.0% |
| `ptclamp=off` L3 | 2.441 | −9.9% |
| `ptreg=off` L6 | 2.458 | −9.2% |
| **`ptbounce=off` L8** | **2.796** | **+3.2%** |

`ptbounce` moves the metric **+14.7%** relative to the bounce-on cluster —
the entire gap and a little past it. `ptclamp` and `ptreg` moved it ~1 pp
each. S1 is unaffected: L8 6.809 sits inside the 6.456–6.809 band that vanilla
and mod already share. **Dim light only, one switch, whole effect.**

### 18.2 …and the sign of the finding flips

§17.3 warned that a high-pass metric cannot separate *removed noise* from
*removed detail*. Three things now say this is noise:

1. **Mechanism.** The bounce cull mask 1→255 (`26` §4) puts far more geometry
   into indirect paths. More contributing geometry means better-converged GI.
2. **Dim light only** — precisely where indirect sampling noise dominates the
   image and where convergence has something to fix.
3. **The user, unprompted, at the launch that identified it:** *"I like PT
   bounce. Like knowing there's more proper path tracing happening. The effect
   is super subtle."*

So the correct description of the whole thread that began at §6.2 is:
**the default stack converges dim-light GI better, and the fine-energy metric
scores that improvement as a 10% loss.** `ptbounce` stays on; the params file
is back at the shipping default.

What died along the way, for the record: §6.2's "the default costs 15.9% of
skin texture" (regime artefact, §13/§14), the `ptclamp` mechanism that
hypothesis spawned (§15), `ptreg` (§16), and every S3-skin figure (§16.2).
What survived is one real, replicated, correctly-signed effect — and it is a
feature.

### 18.3 GOTCHA: the journal's `payload=` is a stat hash, not a content hash

`sync_settings.sh:339` computes it from `stat -c '%n %s %Y'` — name, size,
mtime. `ptq/rcm` and `ptq/rcbm` are different builds (`6fe05ecc3ab345df` vs
`55ed4e5c6884ab71`) whose files share names, sizes and build-run mtimes, so
**both launches logged `payload=225acb871d94a4b8`.** Equal payload does **not**
prove equal bytes served.

Cache eviction is unaffected — it keys off the whole `want` string, which
carries `ptq=$ptq_state` — and `cache=cleared` did fire. But when a launch
must be proven to have served something different, hash the overlay:

```bash
cat ~/.local/lib/callisto/swaps.ptq/*.spv | sha256sum | cut -c1-16
```

Two launches were nearly discarded as "served the same thing" on the strength
of a colliding payload field.

```

`handoff/47-PROCESS-TRACE.md`:

```md
# 47 — Process trace of the 2026-08-30 afternoon A/B session (L1–L8)

**Written for a peer reviewer.** `46` §11–§18 is the *result* record, written
incrementally as each launch landed. This document is the *decision* record:
what I believed at each step, why I chose the next launch, what I predicted,
and where I was wrong. It deliberately preserves reasoning that was later
overturned, in sequence, because the review question is whether the process
was sound — not just whether the surviving numbers are.

Read `46` §18 for where things landed. Read this for how.

Eight launches, 14:45 → 16:53. Two of my conclusions were withdrawn during
the session and one of my launch-queue decisions was reversed. Both failures
have the same cause, called out in §6 below.

---

## 1. Inherited state and the first correction

`46` §1–§10 recorded six launches (E0, E1, E2a `rough-1.3`, E2b `gloss-0.7`,
plus two earlier), peer-reviewed in §9, with a queue L1–L4 defined in §9.4.
The standing claims I was handed:

- `rough-1.3` and `gloss-0.7` add +35% / +48% fine skin texture (§5.2)
- the shipping default *costs* 15.9% of skin texture vs vanilla (§6.2)
- tier-1 `c1` is absent on bounce-lit skin — `42` reopened (§6.1)
- no noise floor had ever been measured

**Pre-flight** (`make check`, ladder inventory, `ser.set` src_sha vs ptq base,
kernel presets, `cmp` of `init.lua` / `pt_engine.lua` / `sync_settings.sh` /
layer `.so`): all clean. One discrepancy — **§10 claimed the params file was
at the E1 config; it was actually at `skinspec=gloss-0.7`** from the 13:50 E2b
launch. Corrected before L1. Minor, but it is the class of thing that silently
mis-attributes a launch, so it is logged.

I also wrote `a-b-testing/collect.sh` (pull the N newest photo-mode captures
into a rung dir in shooting order) because the same pickup was going to happen
four or more times.

---

## 2. L1 — the null relaunch, and the conclusion I got wrong

**Decision.** Run §9.4's L1 unchanged: a byte-identical relaunch of E1, to
measure what two identical launches disagree about. This was the right call
and I would make it again — the project had six launches of published numbers
and zero floor.

**Serve verified** before looking at pixels: `skin_sha=0d0f3ee45ea0d538`,
`payload=225acb871d94a4b8`, 77/12/10/3 HITs, 0 `ser_reject` — identical to E1.

**What I measured (E1 → L1):**

| | S1 | S2 | S3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean `dLum` | +1.232 | −0.061 | −0.020 |
| fine texture | +58.5% | −0.4% | −25.6% |

**What I concluded, and published as §11:** S1 and S3 have a floor larger than
every effect ever measured in them; S2 is the only trustworthy scene. I
rendered difference heatmaps, saw dense pore-scale speckle over the whole face
with flat static controls and 0,0 alignment, and wrote §11.4: *"the floor is
Ray Reconstruction resolving different pores between runs."*

**Consequent queue decisions:** dropped L3 (`ptclamp=off`) on the grounds that
its only motivation — §6.2's −15.9% — was inside the floor; promoted L4 from
one launch to two, so the RR-off *floor* would be measured rather than just
the RR effect.

**This was wrong.** Not the measurement — the two frames really do differ that
much — but the *attribution*. I had two samples and treated their difference
as a property of the process, without asking whether one of the two was
anomalous. See §5.

**What I should have done at this exact point:** run the same texture metric
on a non-skin region of the same frames. It costs one command, it was
available, and it would have shown immediately that sky and terrain had moved
too — which no skin overlay can cause. I did not think of it until L4a forced
it three launches later.

---

## 3. L2 — a static pre-flight that changed the experiment, and a good user catch

### 3.1 The pre-flight find (`46` §12)

Before staging L2 I checked what `skinspec=probe-cls` would actually serve.
**76 modules, where every skin rung has 77.** The missing one was
`ab0bc2fee876d489` — which `46` §9 c2 had named as one of "the two GI
resolvers" and used to *exclude* the "the lift missed the module" hypothesis.

I reproduced the decline (`no image write reachable for the hunt`) and then
disassembled it:

| | `ab0bc2fe` | `99bb7c26` |
|---|---|---|
| sole `OpImageWrite` target | `OpTypeImage %int 2D … 2` | float 2D |
| value written | `v4uint` → `OpBitcast %v4int` | `v4float` |
| components | `OpSelect(valid, RoundEven→ConvertFToS(f), 0xFFFFFFFF)` | radiance |
| guards | `IsInf`/`IsNan`, `ULessThan … 2`, `&255`+1 counter | none |
| workgroup/subgroup | LDS, `%SubgroupSize`, `LocalSize 32 16 1` | none |

Census: **76 of 77 write `v4float`; exactly one writes `v4uint`.**

Conclusion: `ab0bc2fe` is a sample-index / reservoir pass (ReSTIR-shaped),
not a radiance resolver. It matches the (1/π, 0.107508637) anchor because it
evaluates the material stack to compute a reuse *weight*. §9 c2's exclusion
does not hold; there is **one** colour-writing resolver in the anchored set.

**Reasoning about whether this breaks L2.** My first instinct was that L2 had
become a false-negative trap — the probe cannot paint `ab0bc2fe`, so an
unpainted face would be ambiguous. I then rejected that: `ab0bc2fe` has no
colour output at all, so it cannot paint by *any* mechanism and is not a
competing explanation for an unpainted face. L2's negative case is therefore
*cleaner* than §9.4 assumed, not muddier. I ran it.

This is the one step in the session I would hold up as done right: a static
check, costing no launch, that corrected a peer-reviewed claim and sharpened
the experiment before it ran.

### 3.2 The user caught a design flaw

I initially staged L2 as "S2 only", following §9.4 literally. The user asked
*"you just need the S2?"* — and the answer was no. I revised to S1 + S2:

- **S1 is the positive control.** With S2 alone, an unpainted face could mean
  "the gate fails on bounce-lit skin" *or* "the probe didn't work this
  launch". Not separable.
- **S1 answers E5 for free.** The palette paints class 8 violet, and E5's most
  valuable outcome (`45` §3) is finding out whether the eyes are class 8 at
  all.

A single-scene probe launch with no positive control was a real design error
and the user's question is what caught it. Logged as such.

### 3.3 Results and the reading

Serve verified: **dxil ×76** — exactly as §12 predicted — `skin_sha=53722d3d833238ab`.

User's unprompted report: *"S1 showed the red on skin and pink in plants. The
red only shows up from sunlight. S2/3 dont have that colouring."*

Measured, with a non-skin control (which by this point I was using):

| scene | skin px painted beyond the null's p99.9 |
|---|---|
| S1 | **25.8%** |
| S2 | **0.0%** (skin median −0.354, *less* red than non-skin) |
| S3 | **0%** — its +0.131 matched non-skin's +0.119, i.e. global |

S3's apparent paint was the probe tinting GI scene-wide: painted surfaces
bounce painted light onto unpainted ones. Worth remembering for any future
probe launch.

Paint strength vs illumination (S1 skin, R−G of the ratio):

| baseline lum | probe | null |
|---|---|---|
| 11–94 | +0.008 | +0.003 |
| 94–117 | +0.041 | +0.003 |
| **117–139** | **+0.285** | +0.003 |
| **139–209** | **+0.317** | +0.011 |

A step function, not a ramp.

**Conclusion:** the class gate passes on skin — hypothesis (a) is dead — but
the painted modules write only the **direct-light term**. Bounce-lit radiance
comes from a writer outside the painted 76 → **§6.1 hypothesis (b)**. `42`
does not close: the commit *"Skin BRDF was direct-light only: lift the class
gate into the GI resolvers"* did not achieve its goal.

### 3.4 My error on the eyes

I looked at a zoomed eye crop and reported the eyes were **not** violet, and
that E5 was therefore predicted null. The user pushed back: *"eyes have a tint
of violet in them but only from the sun barely clipping them, look again."*

They were right. Quantifying against the null pair:

- 267 px with `B−G > 0.35` vs the null's 132 in the same box
- **30 px above the null's maximum** (+0.893), clustered on both upper lash
  lines, y-band 555–588
- mean L1 `[46.5, 36.9, 15.8]` → L2 `[75.8, 57.2, 44.6]`: **blue ×2.82**
  against the palette's ×3.0, red ×1.63 against ×1.5

A side-by-side against the unpainted launch showed the sclera turning violet
and the lower lashes turning **yellow** (class 4 = hair — a clean internal
consistency check).

**Why I got it wrong:** I judged a sparse, sub-1%-of-pixels effect by eye on a
single crop, when the whole session was otherwise built on measuring against a
null. The correct move was the ratio test first, eyeball second. Note also
that the green channel does *not* fit a clean multiply model (it rises when
paint should crush it), so the 30-px result is real but the model is not
fully explained — a reviewer may want to attack this.

## 4. L4a — the failure that exposed §11

### 4.1 Verification caught it before a second launch was wasted

I staged L4 (RR off) and asked for two launches. After the first, the mod side
verified clean, but the journal cannot see game settings — so I read
`UserSettings.json`: **`DLSS_D: true`**. RR had never been turned off. I told
the user to stop rather than spend the second launch.

This is the verification discipline working. It is also the moment the session
turned, because a third same-config sample was now available.

### 4.2 Three samples beat two

L1 ↔ L4a differed *far less* than E1 ↔ L1:

| pair | S1 mean | S1 fine texture |
|---|---|---|
| E1 → L1 (my "floor") | +1.232 | +58.5% |
| L1 → L4a | +0.166 | +6.1% |

That asymmetry is only explicable if one capture is anomalous. I finally ran
the check I should have run at L1 — **the same metric on non-skin**:

| capture | time | non-skin fine | vs E0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| E0 | 12:59 | 5.881 | — |
| E1 | 13:19 | 5.721 | −2.7% |
| E2a | 13:38 | 6.583 | **+11.9%** |
| E2b | 13:53 | 6.987 | **+18.8%** |
| L1 | 14:47 | 6.600 | **+12.2%** |
| L4a | 15:39 | 6.785 | **+15.4%** |

**Static geometry gained 12–19% fine energy between 13:28 and 13:36 and stayed
there.** No skin overlay can do that. Something changed in the renderer —
most likely a graphics setting (DLSS preset or `DLSS_NewSharpness`, currently
0.25); the settings file stores only current state so the history is gone.

Call pre-13:30 **regime A** (E0, E1) and post-13:30 **regime B** (E2a, E2b,
L1, L2, L4a, and everything after). **Every E1-baselined figure in `46` §5
straddles the break.**

### 4.3 What I withdrew and what I reversed

- **§11.4 withdrawn outright.** "RR resolves different pores" was read off a
  heatmap spanning the break. RR remained untested.
- **§11.1's floor figure withdrawn.** True within-regime floor (L1→L4a): S1
  mean +0.166 / texture +6.1%; S2 +0.043; S3 mean +0.449 / texture +9.3%.
- **E2 rungs re-measured inside regime B, with a non-skin control:**
  skin-specific movement `rough-1.3` +1.4 pp, `gloss-0.7` +5.1 pp, against a
  null-to-null +3.3 pp. **Still dead — but for the right reason** (a ~6% floor
  plus a contaminated baseline, not a 58% floor).
- **§11.3 survived and strengthened**: S2's floor is +0.043 with a
  within-regime null, and the E2a→E2b differential (both regime B) gives a
  flat face with **+3.23%** on the top-3% highlight against a null top-bin of
  −0.95%.
- **L3 reinstated.** I had dropped it using the invalid cross-regime floor.
  §6.2 was *unproven*, not disproven.

---

## 5. The pivot: why I stopped chasing RR and went for vanilla

The user asked, in plain terms, what to do and whether RR should be on. My
answer was: **leave RR on, touch nothing, and shoot vanilla instead.**
Reasoning, in the order it mattered:

1. **Settings changes are what broke the data.** Having just discovered a
   settings-induced regime break, deliberately introducing another one
   mid-investigation was the wrong risk.
2. **The headline question was unmeasurable.** Two mod-default captures
   existed in regime B and zero vanilla ones. "Does the mod change anything
   you can see" could not be answered at all.
3. **Cost asymmetry.** Vanilla is one launch and answers a product question;
   the RR floor is two launches and answers a methodology question.
4. **Ordering.** Do all RR-on work first, then switch deliberately as a block.

I consider this the best decision of the session. It converted a stalled
methodology chase into a chain of five launches that each answered something.

---

## 6. L5 → L8: the elimination chain

Each launch from here carried an **explicit falsifiable prediction written
before it ran**. Two of the three predictions failed, which is why the chain
converged instead of wandering.

### L5 (16:08) — vanilla in regime B

Verified `payload=d2dfb3f53119172b`, 0 HITs — identical fingerprint to the
12:38 E0. Saved by the user into the `L4b-rr-off` dir with `DLSS_D` reading
`false` afterwards, so I had to establish whether RR was off *during* capture:
S1 non-skin **6.581** against L1's **6.600** (0.3%) on a metric where the
regime break moved 12–19%, plus a visually identical terrain crop. **RR was on
during the shots, toggled after.** Refiled as `L5-vanilla-regimeB`.

Results — the first valid mod-vs-vanilla measurement the project has:

| S1 baseline tone | mod effect | floor |
|---|---|---|
| 10.6–88.2 | +0.21…+0.26% | +0.35…+1.14% |
| 88.2–106.4 | +0.43% | +0.14% |
| **106.4–135.1** | **+1.83%** | +0.23% |
| **135.1–166.5** | **+1.66%** | −0.59% |

**The mod brightens only the lit half of the face**, switching on at ~106
luminance — independently reproducing L2's paint threshold of ~116 from a
completely different instrument. S2 at/near floor with the wrong sign for c1
(§6.1 stands). S3: mean −0.478, bright bins −3.91% / −6.90%.

Texture: **S1 skin-specific 0.0 pp and +3.3 pp → the mod costs no skin texture
in direct sun.** §6.2's headline is retired on evidence. S3: non-skin −9.6% /
−9.9%.

**Hypothesis formed:** `ptclamp`. A firefly clamp clips bright outliers, which
in a dim sample-starved scene is most of the high-frequency energy.

### L3 (16:26) — `ptclamp=off`. Prediction FAILED.

Verified `ptq=rbm`, RR on (S1 non-skin 6.667, in band). S3 non-skin **2.441**
against 2.431 / 2.424 with the clamp *on* — **no movement**. The clamp *was*
convicted of dimming (mean vanilla→mod flips −0.478 → +0.153; bright bins
−3.91→−2.30, −6.90→−5.11), but exonerated for the detail loss. §6.2's
mechanism is wrong.

**Next hypothesis:** `ptreg` — path regularization literally trades
high-frequency variance for smoothness.

### L6 (16:37) — `ptreg=off`. Prediction FAILED again.

Verified `ptq=cbm`. S3 non-skin **2.458** — ~1 pp. Cleared.

**Second metric withdrawal, found here.** L1 and L4a (identical config) give
S3 *skin* fine energy **1.574 vs 1.720 — 9.3% apart**, while the same pair
gives S3 non-skin **0.3% apart**. S3's skin mask is small (57,883 px, 23.9% of
crop) on the noisiest surface in the dimmest scene. **Every S3-skin figure in
§14–§15 was inside its own floor** and was withdrawn, including the
"skin loses 11–18 pp beyond the scene-wide loss" claim I had made two steps
earlier. S3 non-skin stands.

**Decision point.** Four mod samples now clustered within 1.4%; vanilla sat
+10.3% above — on **one** sample. I applied the rule I had written into
`GOTCHAS` that same afternoon (*a rung is not measured until a null relaunch
of the same config has been measured*) and spent the next launch on repeating
the baseline rather than continuing elimination. Given §11 had just been
withdrawn for exactly this error, continuing would have been indefensible.

### L7 (16:45) — vanilla repeat. The effect is real.

| | n | mean | spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla (L5, L7) | 2 | 2.708 | 1.4% |
| mod (L1, L4a, L3, L6) | 4 | 2.438 | 1.4% |

Difference **−9.9%**, **7.3×** the larger within-cluster spread, **no
overlap** (vanilla min 2.689 > mod max 2.458). Dim light only — S1 shows
vanilla 6.581/6.456 against mod 6.600/6.785, fully overlapping.

**Next hypothesis, on mechanism rather than elimination:** `ptbounce`. The
bounce cull mask 1→255 puts far more geometry into indirect paths → better
converged GI → an effect that appears only where indirect light dominates.

I also wrote the noise-vs-detail caveat into §17.3 *before* the launch, and
asked the user for an eye verdict at the same launch that identified the
switch — specifically so the interpretation would not be decided afterwards by
whoever liked their own hypothesis.

### L8 (16:53) — `ptbounce=off`. Confirmed.

**A near-miss first.** Journal read `ptq=rcm` but `payload=225acb871d94a4b8`
— identical to the default's. I almost discarded the launch as a
non-serve. Checking the overlay content directly: `swaps.ptq` hashed
`6fe05ecc3ab345df` = `ptq/rcm/base`. Correct serve. The payload field is
computed from `stat -c '%n %s %Y'` (name/size/mtime), so two different builds
with equal sizes and build-run mtimes collide. **Equal payload does not prove
equal bytes.** New `GOTCHAS` rule; cache eviction is unaffected (it keys off
the whole `want` string).

Result: S3 non-skin **2.796** — above *both* vanilla samples, **+14.7%** vs
the bounce-on cluster. One switch spans the entire gap. S1 unaffected.

**And the sign flips.** The user's verdict, given before knowing which switch
was under test: *"I like PT bounce. Like knowing there's more proper path
tracing happening. The effect is super subtle."* Combined with the mechanism
and the dim-light-only signature, the honest description is **the mod
converges dim-light GI better, and the fine-energy metric scores that
improvement as a 10% loss.** `ptbounce` stays on; params restored to default.

---

## 7. Where the results stand

**Replicated on both sides, surviving:**

- `ptbounce` converges dim-light GI: −9.9% scene-wide fine energy, 2 vanilla
  vs 4 mod samples, no overlap, one switch spans it. Interpreted as
  improvement (§18.2).
- The skin BRDF reaches **directly-lit skin only**. Two independent
  instruments, one threshold: paint probe ~116 lum, radiometric ~106.
- `42` does **not** close. The GI radiance writer for skin is not among the 77
  anchored modules.
- `ab0bc2fe` writes integer sample indices, not colour (§12); §9 c2 corrected.
- Material classes: skin 1, hair 4 (incl. eyelashes), plants 5, eyes 8.
- S2 is a low-floor scene (+0.043 mean, −0.4% texture); §6.1's S2 null is real.
- E2a→E2b differential: flat face, **+3.23%** top-3% highlight vs −0.95% null.

**Dead or withdrawn:**

| claim | why |
|---|---|
| §5.2 E2 texture gains (+35%/+48%) | cross-regime baseline; re-measured in regime B they are inside the floor |
| §5.1 E2 means (+1.40%/+1.37%) | same |
| §6.2 "default costs 15.9% of skin texture" | regime artefact; L5 shows 0.0 pp skin-specific in S1 |
| the `ptclamp` mechanism | L3: no movement |
| `ptreg` as a cause | L6: ~1 pp |
| §11.1 floor figure, §11.4 RR mechanism | §13: it was the regime break |
| all S3-**skin** texture figures | §16.2: 9.3% same-config floor |

**Metric reliability, measured (same-config floors):** S3 non-skin **0.3%**,
S1 non-skin **~3%**, S1 skin **~6%**, S3 skin **~9%**. Region choice matters
more than metric choice.

**Still open:** the real L4 (RR off, two launches — RR has never actually been
tested); the roughness fork (still `rough-1.3`, on the user's eye and the `33`
§2 wet-plastic argument, not on numbers); finding the GI radiance writer
(a static search, no launch needed); the probe legend decode (`45` E11).

---

## 8. Self-critique

**Both of my withdrawn conclusions have one cause: I trusted an unreplicated
baseline.** §11 treated E1 as a valid second sample of its own config; §14–§15
treated L5 as a valid vanilla baseline and computed skin-specific figures off
an S3-skin metric whose floor I had not measured. Both produced *confident*
wrong answers with mechanisms attached — §11.4 named Ray Reconstruction,
§14.3 named the firefly clamp — which is worse than a hedge, because a named
mechanism invites the next person to test it. In the clamp's case that is
exactly what happened, and it cost a launch.

The corrective that worked, both times, was the same and was cheap: **a
control region that the manipulation cannot affect**, and **a repeat of the
baseline**. Neither needed new tooling. I had `--mask` inversion available
from the first minute.

Ranked, my errors:

1. **§11's floor attribution** — the largest. Caused a wrong queue decision
   (dropping L3) that took three launches to reverse.
2. **§11.4's RR mechanism claim** — a causal story from a confounded pair.
3. **S3-skin figures in §14–§15** — quoted a metric whose floor I had not
   measured, in the same session in which I wrote a rule about exactly that.
4. **The eyes** — judged a sub-1% effect by eye instead of by ratio test;
   corrected by the user.
5. **L2 staged without a positive control** — caught by the user's question.
6. **Nearly discarding L8** on a colliding payload field.

What I would keep: verifying the serve before reading any pixel (it caught the
RR-still-on case before the second launch was wasted); the static pre-flight
that produced §12; writing falsifiable predictions before each launch; and
asking for the user's visual verdict at the same launch that identified the
switch, rather than after the interpretation was already leaning.

---

## 9. Where a reviewer should attack this first

Ordered by how much rests on them.

1. **The regime break is uncharacterised.** I never identified what changed at
   ~13:30, only that it did. Regime membership for every later capture is
   asserted from the S1 non-skin band (6.456–6.809). If a second, smaller
   break occurred inside regime B, the L5→L8 cluster comparison would absorb
   it silently. Test: re-derive the break using an independent statistic
   (e.g. mid/coarse bands, or a sky-only crop) and check it partitions the
   captures the same way.
2. **RR state during capture is inferred, never observed.** `UserSettings.json`
   records only state at process exit, and the user toggled RR repeatedly
   *after* shooting. For L5, L6, L7, L8 I concluded "RR was on" from S1
   non-skin sitting in-band. If that inference is wrong for even one capture,
   the vanilla and mod clusters are mixed and §17's separation is unsafe.
3. **The mod "cluster" of n=4 mixes three configs.** L3 and L6 differ from
   default by one switch each, and each switch was independently shown to move
   the metric ~1 pp. Pooling them tightens the apparent spread. A stricter
   reading uses only L1 and L4a (n=2, 2.431/2.424) against L5 and L7 (n=2,
   2.689/2.726) — still separated, but with n=2 on both sides.
4. **L8 exceeds vanilla** (2.796 vs 2.689/2.726) and I did not explain it. If
   `ptbounce=off` returns to vanilla behaviour, why is it higher? n=1.
5. **"Noise, not detail" is an inference, not a measurement.** It rests on
   mechanism + dim-light-only + one user preference. Nothing measured
   separates converged noise from authored detail. A real test exists
   (frame-to-frame variance at a fixed camera) and was not run.
6. **The two-instrument threshold agreement (~116 vs ~106)** uses different
   metrics with different bin edges. The agreement may be looser than §5
   presents it.
7. **The eye class-8 result is 30 pixels**, and its green channel contradicts
   a pure multiply model. Real, but thin.
8. **S2's old-character caveat still stands** (`46` §6.1). I tested whether a
   current-character E0→E1 S2 pair existed and it does not — SSD 283 vs the
   null's 6.7, controls swinging ±3 with sd 20. §6.1 still rests on the
   old-character pair.

## 11. Peer review of this trace (2026-08-30 late evening, second Fable pass)

**Method.** Every load-bearing figure re-derived from the captures, not from

vanilla, 2.431/2.424/2.441/2.458 mod, 2.796 bounce-off), §14.1's tone bins

`LAUNCHES.md` was regenerated for all 14 launches — it had been stale at 7,
so the serve record for L2–L8 existed only in the journal. The regenerated
record independently confirms two claims: the 15:11 L2 row reads **dxil ×76
/ 104 HITs** (§12's census, from the layer's own log), and the 16:53 L8 row
shows `payload=225acb871d94a4b8` beside `ptq=rcm` (§18.3's collision, now
